A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original SAE experiments on ImageNet and MNIST, vision and language-model scaling studies, and supplementary experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–2, the scaling studies, and the appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The TTT procedures, SAE architectures, adaptive masking objective, and language-model LoRA adaptation are unchanged. Equations 1–2 and Appendix F specify the same methods.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ImageNet and MNIST classification tasks and Pile language-modeling coverage. The appendices introduce no additional datasets or test scenarios in v4.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, including global training and majority voting, the full-model versus linear-head TTT comparison in Appendix D.2, and the MoE comparison in Appendix F.5.

E3.justification: The versions specify identical splits, metrics, model scales, neighborhood sizes, optimization budgets, and evaluation procedures. This includes the settings and hyperparameters documented in Appendices D–F and Tables 3–10.

E4.justification: Both retain the same masking and prediction-agreement analyses, neighborhood-size study, global evaluation of local heads, end-to-end TTT comparison, and ImageNet cross-entropy analysis. No ablation or supplementary analysis is added or revised.

E5.justification: Both retain 90% bootstrap confidence intervals, bootstrap standard errors in Tables 1–2, and five-seed MNIST experiments with 200 bootstrap iterations per seed. No statistical reporting practice or run count changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings match throughout. For example, Table 2 reports ImageNet accuracy of 78.33% for global training and 79.39% for TTT on the test sample in both versions. Appendix result entries are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 5 and Appendices A–C retain the same definitions, assumptions, sparse-recovery bounds, global-training construction, and proofs. Differences in mathematical glyphs and appendix references are typographic.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same specialization-after-generalization claim: TTT can improve in-distribution predictions under global underparameterization, with diminishing benefits as model capacity increases.

C2.justification: The explanations involving sparse concepts, interference, local specialization, and neighborhood tradeoffs are unchanged. Qualifications concerning idealized assumptions, noise, applicability, and future research are also retained.

D1.justification: Implementation details, preprocessing, hyperparameters, hardware disclosures, and code-access statements are unchanged. The new acknowledgments disclose support and funding without adding technical reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including comparisons with local learning, non-parametric methods, sparse autoencoders, and mixtures of experts. The reference list is reflowed without changing its membership.

P1.justification: v4 adds acknowledgments before the references, replaces the preprint header with an ICLR 2026 publication header, changes appendix references from 'Section' to 'Appendix', and makes a small wording edit. The scientific narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The acknowledgments change page 10's layout and reflow the references and subsequent pagination. Running headers and some caption wrapping change, while all nine figures and ten tables retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: v4 adds acknowledgments and standardizes appendix references. The methods, empirical evidence, proofs, interpretations, and reproducibility documentation remain unchanged. These limited editorial and layout changes do not materially alter clarity or evidential strength, leaving overall quality effectively the same.
